items.q: First line maintenance therapy for chronic idiopathic constipation is which class?
o: Daily senna indefinitely as sole plan
items.exp: Macrogols safely hold luminal water long term with minimal electrolyte shifts and strong evidence, while stimulants serve as rescue additions. Antidiarrhoeals cause the opposite of the goal.
r: Incorrect. Stimulants are rescue, not the backbone.
Correct. Osmotic macrogols lead chronic care.
Incorrect. Loperamide constipates by design.
Incorrect. Paraffin risks lipoid pneumonia and vitamin malabsorption.

items.q: Lactulose improves hepatic encephalopathy mainly by doing what?
o: Acidifying colon so ammonia is trapped as ammonium and expelled
items.exp: Colonic bacteria ferment lactulose to acids; low pH converts diffusible ammonia to trapped ammonium while osmotic catharsis expels it, lowering cerebral ammonia load.
r: Incorrect. Antibacterial effect is secondary to acid trapping.
Correct. Acidification traps ammonia in stool.
Incorrect. No cerebral receptor blockade occurs.
Incorrect. Bilirubin handling is unrelated to encephalopathy relief.
items.kp: Lactulose acidifies, traps ammonia, purges it.

items.q: Antimotility loperamide must be avoided in which diarrhoea presentation?
o: Bloody diarrhoea with fever and suspected invasive infection
items.exp: Slowing transit in invasive or toxin mediated colitis retains organisms and toxins, risking toxic megacolon and perforation, so bloody febrile diarrhoea forbids antimotility agents.
r: Incorrect. Uncomplicated watery diarrhoea may use it briefly.
Correct. Bloody and febrile means never slow the gut.
Incorrect. Bile acid diarrhoea uses sequestrants mainly.
Incorrect. IBS diarrhoea may cautiously use loperamide.
items.kp: Blood plus fever: hands off loperamide.

items.q: Opioid induced constipation failing osmotics may need methylnaltrexone because it blocks what?
o: Peripheral gut mu receptors without crossing into brain
items.exp: Methylnaltrexone is a quaternary mu antagonist confined peripherally, restoring gut motility while sparing central analgesia, unlike naloxone which can reverse pain control.
r: Incorrect. Central reversal would destroy analgesia and is avoided.
Correct. Peripheral blockade moves gut, spares pain relief.
Incorrect. Serotonin pathways are prucalopride territory.
Incorrect. Channel blockade is not its mechanism.
items.kp: Block gut opioids, spare brain analgesia.

items.q: Mesalazine (5-ASA) is the therapeutic backbone for which condition?
items.exp: Topically acting aminosalicylates induce and maintain remission in ulcerative colitis, delivered orally and rectally by disease extent, with weak inconsistent benefit in Crohn disease.
r: Incorrect. Fistulising Crohn needs biologics and surgery pathways.
Correct. Ulcerative colitis is mesalazine territory.
Incorrect. IBS lacks mucosal inflammation to suppress.
Incorrect. Coeliac therapy is gluten exclusion.

items.q: Steroids in IBD are properly used how?
o: To induce remission in flares, never as maintenance
As first line for mild proctitis
items.exp: Steroids rapidly induce remission but do not maintain it or heal mucosa durably, while their metabolic, bone and infection harms forbid chronic maintenance roles.
r: Incorrect. Maintenance steroids are a prescribing error.
Correct. Induce only, then hand over to maintainers.
Incorrect. Systemic steroids rescue severe flares legitimately.
Incorrect. Mild proctitis starts with rectal mesalazine.
items.kp: Steroids open the door; they cannot hold it.

items.q: Before starting anti TNF therapy for Crohn disease, mandatory screening includes what?
o: Latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B assessment
items.exp: TNF blockade can reactivate latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B, so chest imaging, interferon gamma testing and hepatitis serology precede therapy with vaccination review.
r: Incorrect. Endoscopy stages disease but misses infection risk.
Correct. TB and hepatitis screening are mandatory.
Incorrect. Bone health matters with steroids, not the gate here.
Incorrect. Metabolite testing belongs to thiopurines.
items.kp: No anti TNF without TB screening.

items.q: Thiopurine therapy (azathioprine) in IBD requires vigilance for which late malignancy signal?
o: Non melanoma skin cancer and lymphoma risk
items.exp: Chronic thiopurine immunosuppression raises non melanoma skin cancer and lymphoma (including rare fatal hepatosplenic T cell lymphoma in young males), demanding sun protection and counselling.
r: Incorrect. Lung cancer is smoking driven, not the thiopurine signal.
Correct. Skin cancers and lymphoma rise on thiopurines.
Incorrect. Thyroid cancer is not the class warning.
Incorrect. Prostate risk is not thiopurine linked.
items.kp: Azathioprine years later: watch skin and lymphoma.

items.q: The actual life saving treatment in acute cholera diarrhoea alongside antibiotics is what?
items.exp: Profuse secretory losses kill by dehydration and electrolytes; rehydration replaces them and saves life, while antimotility drugs neither replace fluid nor shorten toxin clearance safely.
r: Incorrect. Motility drugs cannot replace lost litres.
Correct. Rehydration is the life saver.
Incorrect. Codeine adds ileus risk without fluid benefit.
Incorrect. Surgery has no role in secretory diarrhoea.
items.kp: Diarrhoea kills by dehydration; rehydrate first.

items.q: Senna is best timed and used how in constipation care?
o: Night dose as rescue when osmotics stall, effect by morning
items.exp: Stimulant laxatives act after colonic bacterial activation over six to twelve hours, so a night dose produces morning evacuation and serves as rescue layered on osmotic maintenance.
r: Incorrect. Its onset is hours, not immediate.
Correct. Night dosing, morning result, rescue role.
Incorrect. Hourly dosing invites cramps and electrolytes loss.
Incorrect. Oral senna is standard; enemas are separate tools.
items.kp: Senna at night, result in the morning.
